messages.subject: Simple Sub-setting / Match() Question
parts:
Hi, I'm struggling with a simple sub-setting issue.  Many thanks for all guidance!  


SAMPLE DATA:

admissions (it's a data.table: case_no and diagnosis1-3 are character, LOS is an integer)

case_no, diagnosis1, diagnosis2, LOS, diagnosis3, 
100567, 0700, 0894, 19, 0052
100568, 9847, 0300, 4, 4011
100569, 3187, 8751, 2, 0500



septicemia: "0380"  "0381"  "0382"  "0383"  "0384"  "03840" (all character)



I'd like to subset admissions by matching any of the values in diagnosis1, diagnosis2, or diagnosis3 to any values in septicemia (i.e. I only want to look at admissions with a diagnosis of sepsis).  How do I modify the code below to consider all the diagnosis columns, not just the first one?  I thought about apply, but then I realized that it won't work with a data.table.  

match(septicemia, admissions$diagnosis1, no match = NA_integer_, incomparables = NULL)

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Simple Sub-setting / Match() Question
parts:
Actually, I think I may understand what you mean. I've created a dataframe of some random letters that is analogous to your diagnosis columns. You want to subset to keep rows where any of some columns (all in this example) where any of these columns has that value. So:

> # make fake data
> d <- data.frame(x1=sample(letters[1:10], 10, replace=TRUE),
                            x2=sample(letters[1:10], 10, replace=TRUE),
                            x3=sample(letters[1:10], 10, replace=TRUE))

> vec <- c('a', 'c', 'g') # vector of keep (e.g. your septicemia)
> lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec) # loop across columns, indicating which entries are in vec
$x1
 [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE

$x2
 [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE

$x3
 [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
> do.call(cbind, lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec))  # bind these all up into a dataframe
         x1    x2    x3
 [1,]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
 [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [3,]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
 [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [5,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [6,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [7,] FALSE  TRUE FALSE
 [8,]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE
 [9,] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE
[10,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
> apply(do.call(cbind, lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec)), 1, any)  # now, if any of col's values in vec, keep
 [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

Now you have an indexing vector:

> i <- apply(do.call(cbind, lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec)), 1, any)
> d[i, ]
  x1 x2 x3
1  c  e  j
3  g  g  a
7  j  c  e
8  a  e  g
9  i  a  c

You may need to coerce your data.table to a data.frame, but this is the idea. I think there might be a simpler way, but this is a good first approximation to get the problem solved and move forward. 

Of course you don't need to do the whole lapply() stuff — you could do this by writing out all the logical comparisons, but I don't like tedious things like that.

Hope this helps,
V

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Simple Sub-setting / Match() Question
parts:
This solution should work if you don’t have too many diagnosis columns, and it should work with data.table speed on a data table:

admissions[diagnosis1 %in% septicemia | diagnosis2 %in% septicemia | diagnosis3 %in% septicemia,]

The pipes (“|”) are OR logical operators so we’re asking for rows where Condition 1 OR Condition 2 OR Condition 3 are ment. Also, I’m using the %in% syntax for match() here. x %in% table is equivalent to match(x, table).

​

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Simple Sub-setting / Match() Question
parts:
I thought about using apply() directly as you did, but I think in general it's wise to try to avoid it. apply() will always coerce any non-array object with dimensions (e.g. a dataframe) to a matrix using as.matrix() first — and I try to avoid as many implicit coercions as possible (I've been bitten in the past by this). But in this case, as.matrix() on these columns will return a character vector matrix so it should be safe (but maybe not a good general approach).

This approach would be faster (if speed is an issue). Using any() rather than sum() should be faster (I believe any() short circuit evaluates — anyone know for sure?).

Vince

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Simple Sub-setting / Match() Question
parts: Thank you all for your replies.  I learned a lot from them, and I now have functioning code.

On Wednesday, February 25, 2015 at 5:50:25 PM UTC-8, Vince S. Buffalo wrote:
I thought about using apply() directly as you did, but I think in general it's wise to try to avoid it. apply() will always coerce any non-array object with dimensions (e.g. a dataframe) to a matrix using as.matrix() first — and I try to avoid as many implicit coercions as possible (I've been bitten in the past by this). But in this case, as.matrix() on these columns will return a character vector matrix so it should be safe (but maybe not a good general approach).

This approach would be faster (if speed is an issue). Using any() rather than sum() should be faster (I believe any() short circuit evaluates — anyone know for sure?).

Vince

If you are already going to coerce to a data.frame, why not:

septicemia <- c("0380", "0381", "0382", "0383", "0384", "03840")

idx <- apply(df[, c("diagnosis1", "diagnosis2", "diagnosis3")], MARGIN=1, FUN=function(x)(sum(x %in% septicemia) > 0))

admissions[idx, ]

On Feb 25, 2015, at 4:57 PM, Vince S. Buffalo <vsbu...@gmail.com> wrote:

Actually, I think I may understand what you mean. I've created a dataframe of some random letters that is analogous to your diagnosis columns. You want to subset to keep rows where any of some columns (all in this example) where any of these columns has that value. So:

> # make fake data
> d <- data.frame(x1=sample(letters[1:10], 10, replace=TRUE),
                            x2=sample(letters[1:10], 10, replace=TRUE),
                            x3=sample(letters[1:10], 10, replace=TRUE))

> vec <- c('a', 'c', 'g') # vector of keep (e.g. your septicemia)
> lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec) # loop across columns, indicating which entries are in vec
$x1
 [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE

$x2
 [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE

$x3
 [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
> do.call(cbind, lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec))  # bind these all up into a dataframe
         x1    x2    x3
 [1,]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
 [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [3,]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
 [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [5,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [6,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
 [7,] FALSE  TRUE FALSE
 [8,]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE
 [9,] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE
[10,] FALSE FALSE FALSE
> apply(do.call(cbind, lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec)), 1, any)  # now, if any of col's values in vec, keep
 [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

Now you have an indexing vector:

> i <- apply(do.call(cbind, lapply(d, function(x) x %in% vec)), 1, any)
> d[i, ]
  x1 x2 x3
1  c  e  j
3  g  g  a
7  j  c  e
8  a  e  g
9  i  a  c

You may need to coerce your data.table to a data.frame, but this is the idea. I think there might be a simpler way, but this is a good first approximation to get the problem solved and move forward. 

Of course you don't need to do the whole lapply() stuff — you could do this by writing out all the logical comparisons, but I don't like tedious things like that.

Hope this helps,
V

On Wed, Feb 25, 2015 at 4:19 PM, Mallory Johnson <nie...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, I'm struggling with a simple sub-setting issue.  Many thanks for all guidance!  


SAMPLE DATA:

admissions (it's a data.table: case_no and diagnosis1-3 are character, LOS is an integer)

case_no, diagnosis1, diagnosis2, LOS, diagnosis3, 
100567, 0700, 0894, 19, 0052
100568, 9847, 0300, 4, 4011
100569, 3187, 8751, 2, 0500



septicemia: "0380"  "0381"  "0382"  "0383"  "0384"  "03840" (all character)



I'd like to subset admissions by matching any of the values in diagnosis1, diagnosis2, or diagnosis3 to any values in septicemia (i.e. I only want to look at admissions with a diagnosis of sepsis).  How do I modify the code below to consider all the diagnosis columns, not just the first one?  I thought about apply, but then I realized that it won't work with a data.table.  

match(septicemia, admissions$diagnosis1, no match = NA_integer_, incomparables = NULL)
